notes: A privately funded, landscape-scale restoration inside an SSSI that NRW will regulate and may partner on; it tests how rewilding sits alongside upland farming and counts towards the SI2 restoration rate.
summary: Nation.Cymru reported on 10 February 2026 that the rewilding charity Tir Natur had acquired the 1,195-acre Cwm Doethie site in the Elenydd (Cambrian Mountains), Ceredigion, for Wales' largest rewilding project, using a philanthropic bridging loan after raising over half of the 2.2 million pound cost. The land lies within the Mynydd Mallaen and Cwm Doethie Site of Special Scientific Interest; the charity planned conservation grazing with hardy cattle and ponies and peatland rewetting over five to ten years. A further report in August 2026 recorded cattle returning to the site.
title: Tir Natur buys 1,195 acres at Cwm Doethie in the Cambrian Mountains for Wales' largest rewilding project
